papers.title: Mouse bio-behavioral phenotyping using a digital homecage framework for long-timescale, high-resolution, and multi-factor data collection and analytics.
papers.summary: The authors present the Digital Homecage (DHC), an open-source platform for continuous long-term monitoring of over 20 behavioral metrics in single-housed mice using video, operant tasks, and wheel-running. Initial data validated its ability to capture circadian patterns across spontaneous behaviors, consistently reflecting nocturnal activity.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.summary: This high-definition review evaluates evidence that acupuncture modulates sleep microarchitecture (EEG spectral power, spindles, slow oscillations), finding that direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is very limited and mainly indirect from wake or anesthesia studies. It distinguishes observed findings from hypotheses and outlines pathways and future research requirements.

papers.title: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain.
papers.summary: Using mouse brain-wide synapse mapping, the study shows that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation cause large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations across more than one hundred brain regions. Different experiences modified distinct synapse types and subtypes, supporting a population-selection model of synaptome adaptation shared across development and adulthood.

papers.title: Thalamic Reticular Nucleus Excitability and Cholinergic Signaling are Disrupted in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: In slice electrophysiology from APP transgenic versus control mice, the authors found age-dependent increases in thalamic reticular nucleus excitability and region-specific firing properties, with cholinergic activation suppressing TRN firing. In APP mice, core TRN neurons showed reduced intrinsic excitability and a larger muscarinic inhibitory component that delayed firing, implicating intrinsic and cholinergic mechanisms in early Alzheimer's disease-related TRN dysfunction.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 24 studies on in-ear EEG technology, synthesizing progress in device miniaturization and wearable design and applications including sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload, fatigue, and emotion recognition. The review identifies persistent challenges in signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artifacts requiring validation for broader clinical and real-world use.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation differentially recruits amygdala subregions in male and female mice
papers.summary: Using whole-brain clearing and automated c-Fos counting in wildtype mice, the authors mapped amygdala subnuclei activation after 4-h sleep deprivation (SD) with or without 2-h recovery sleep. SD produced sex-specific patterns: widespread subnuclear activation in males that largely reversed with recovery, versus selective activation of the anterior basolateral and intercalated amygdala in females that persisted after recovery.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.summary: The study applied a pre-registered three-criterion validation framework to 18 EEG features across three independent cohorts to screen candidate amyotrophic lateral sclerosis biomarkers. Gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy met all three criteria (cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, cross-cohort effect consistency), and permutation testing found no permuted three-cohort reliability intersection (Monte Carlo p = 0.001), though bootstrap resampling showed sensitivity of the selected set to sample composition.

papers.title: Regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences exceed longitudinal changes across an approximately 34-h protocol: a prospective quality-controlled proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
papers.summary: In a prospective quality-controlled 1H-MRS study of 138 participants scanned about 34 h apart, regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences were larger and more robust than longitudinal changes, with a median absolute paired standardized effect size of 0.571 for region versus 0.125 for longitudinal change. PCC showed higher NAA/Cr and SVS GlxT/Cr, while ACC showed higher Cho/Cr and MEGA Glu/Cr; follow-up reductions surviving FDR correction were confined to SVS Cr2/Cr and GlxT/Cr.

papers.title: Recovering Resting-State EEG During AM-tACS Using Dynamic Adaptive Stimulation Artifact Source Separation.
papers.summary: The authors developed DASASS, a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework combining recursive covariance updating, adaptive component selection, and wavelet-based multiband processing to recover resting-state EEG during amplitude-modulated tACS. DASASS achieved the lowest normalized root mean square error and demodulated residual modulation among tested methods and preserved four canonical microstate topographies with spatial correlation coefficients of 0.8643–0.9412 relative to artifact-free reference EEG.

papers.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: In 84 nondemented Parkinson's disease patients and 30 healthy older adults, the authors examined sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) during wakefulness using EEG. SLSWs occurred more frequently in PD, and higher SLSW amplitude over frontocentral regions was associated with hallucinatory traits, while more prominent SLSWs were linked to poorer cognition.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.summary: This uncontrolled pilot study compared resting-state EEG in 6–8-year-old children with autism spectrum disorder (n=20) and typically developing children (n=15), and examined pre-post changes around a single 30-min Berard auditory integration training session using FOOOF spectral parameterization. At baseline, ASD showed higher delta and lower theta, alpha, and beta relative power; post-session, delta decreased and beta/gamma increased, while aperiodic exponent and offset showed no significant changes.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: The authors developed an integrated Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform and machine-learning framework using single-channel EEG features (approximate entropy, rhythm energy ratio, C0-complexity, zero-crossing rate) with representative channel selection. Under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, Decision Tree classifiers achieved accuracies of 84.52% (F4) for schizophrenia, 86.54% (F4) for Parkinson's disease, and 93.10% (Fp1) for depression.

papers.title: Sleep starts: Phenomenology and associations with sleep, psychological, and demographic characteristics.
papers.summary: An online survey characterized sleep starts (SS) phenomenology and exploratory associations with demographic, sleep, and psychological measures in 194 adults, separating a high-frequency SS group (n=96) from comparisons (n=98). The SS group reported poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety/depressive symptoms, with sleep quality, dysfunctional beliefs, and anxiety associated with SS frequency in regression models.

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The authors propose SGA-MVTN, a two-stage EEG emotion-recognition framework combining a prior-constrained Multi-View Tower Network with a Structured Genetic Algorithm for topology-aware channel selection. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, full-channel MVTN reached 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV, while SGA-MVTN removed 54.84% of channels while retaining 95.56% of full-channel accuracy.

papers.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
papers.summary: Using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats, four brief intermittent carotid body stimulations with sodium cyanide produced a prolonged (>20 min) increase in inspiratory and late expiratory respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, Traube-Hering waves, and perfusion pressure, effects prevented by carotid sinus denervation. The findings indicate acute intermittent carotid body activation induces long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling relevant to hypertension pathogenesis.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG during a dot-perspective task, this study compared neural generators of altercentric and egocentric biases in healthy controls (n=24) and forensic BPD patients (n=14). In BPD, no significant differential activation was observed, suggesting decreased ability to mobilize brain resources for self-other discrepancy, though limited power requires confirmation.

papers.title: Who gets enough sleep? - Sleep duration and classification based on sleep recommendations among the adult population in Germany.
papers.summary: Using GEDA 2023 telephone survey data, this study estimated mean sleep duration and adherence to National Sleep Foundation recommendations among adults in Germany, stratified by gender, age, and education. Mean sleep was 07:26 hours per night, and 51.6% met recommendations, more often on weekends (54.7% vs 46.7% on weekdays) and among those with higher education (62.5%), with later bedtimes associated with lower adherence.

papers.title: Sleep duration and systemic inflammation assessed using the systemic inflammation response index: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020 and 2021-2023.
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: In cross-sectional NHANES 2017–2020 and 2021–2023 data (10,971 adults), longer weekday sleep within the ≥7 h range was associated with a higher systemic inflammation response index (0.0371 per additional hour, 95% CI 0.0198–0.0544) in pooled exploratory models, but period-specific survey-weighted and log-scale analyses were not uniformly significant. The authors emphasize these findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality or an optimal sleep duration.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: clinical assessment, treatable syndromes, and limits of biomarker inference.
papers.summary: This narrative review links sleep and circadian assessment in Alzheimer's disease to indication-based care, distinguishing symptomatic benefit, physiological target engagement, and disease modification. It covers actigraphy, melatonin timing and temperature rhythms, polysomnography, and quantitative EEG, and organizes clinical priorities such as obstructive sleep apnea, cognition-adapted insomnia care, irregular sleep timing, and excessive daytime sleepiness.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.summary: This dual between-groups and within-subjects EEG study compared long-term Tibetan Buddhist practitioners of Tantra (n=21) and Sutra (n=20) meditation in monastery settings. The Tantra group showed consistently lower alpha power across meditation and baseline conditions, and only the Tantra group showed increased individual alpha peak frequency in occipital leads during meditation, followed by a decrease afterward.

papers.title: Quantitative effects of sleep deprivation on digital pupillary dynamics and visual evoked potential metrics in healthy adults.
papers.journal: International journal of occupational medicine and environmental health
papers.summary: In 18 healthy adults under controlled 48-hour sleep deprivation, pupillary light reflex dilation-phase parameters (DDil1, DDil2) and the VEP N145 component latency/amplitude were identified as sensitive biomarkers of fatigue, corroborated by the pupillary sleepiness test and Stanford Sleepiness Scale. The dilation-phase measures complemented established fatigue indices such as constriction velocity and relative amplitude.

papers.title: Pharmacotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence through June 2026 on pharmacotherapy for the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD—major depressive disorder, sleep disturbances including insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea, alcohol use disorders, and psychoses—and concludes that medication choice must be highly individualized because agents used for PTSD largely do not treat comorbid symptoms.

papers.title: A volumetric threshold and age-dependent remodeling are associated with residual obstructive sleep apnea after adenotonsillectomy in children.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 238 children with OSA undergoing adenotonsillectomy, postoperative upper-airway volume below 10.5 cm³ (AUC=0.89) and younger age independently predicted residual OSA. Complete resolution occurred in 63.4%, and age-dependent soft-tissue remodeling was implicated in persistent disease.

papers.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations.
papers.summary: Using two-wave cross-lagged panel network analysis in 538 adolescents, this study found that depressive symptoms consistently predicted later Internet gaming disorder symptoms, with no reverse cross-disorder pathways, and identified suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms as bridge symptoms. Sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence, and network patterns were broadly similar but not identical across genders.

papers.title: [Epilepsy and Alcohol].
papers.journal: Brain and nerve = Shinkei kenkyu no shinpo
papers.summary: Review of the complex relationship between alcohol consumption and epilepsy, covering acute alcohol effects, alcohol withdrawal seizures, and provocation of seizures in people with epilepsy by heavy or binge drinking combined with sleep deprivation, poor antiseizure medication adherence, dehydration, or metabolic disturbances. Discusses differential diagnosis of alcohol-related versus withdrawal versus acute symptomatic seizures and benzodiazepine-based acute management of withdrawal seizures.

papers.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy in non-NF1 RASopathies: a two-centre retrospective paediatric cohort and scoping review.
papers.summary: Characterized drug-resistant epilepsy in non-NF1 RASopathies using a scoping review (48 eligible records from 435 screened) plus a two-centre retrospective paediatric cohort of six patients (two Noonan syndrome, four cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome with MAP2K1 variants). Reports that DRE is uncommon in Noonan syndrome but frequent and severe in CFC syndrome with polymorphic seizures, status epilepticus, and evidence of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: Retrospective Pediatric Health Information System cohort (2016–2025) of 13,202 neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation, examining institutional variation in EEG utilization and its association with outcomes. EEG monitoring occurred in 12.5% overall, rose from ~6% to >14% over time, and varied widely across hospitals (0% to >40%); EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection, longer length of stay, and higher hospitalization costs.

papers.title: Epidemiology, Complications, and Management of Complications of Achondroplasia: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic literature review and meta-analysis of 200 studies characterized the clinical burden of achondroplasia, reporting prevalence estimates from 1 to 67 per 100,000 births and common complications including sleep disordered breathing (mean 60%), cervicomedullary compression (mean 34%), and kyphosis (mean 43%). It highlights the high frequency and severity of complications and the need for effective treatments.

papers.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence that Parkinson's disease is preceded by a reversible phase of dopaminergic hyperactivation (increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction) manifesting as early non-motor symptoms. Argues this pre-degenerative stage is detectable with multimodal biomarkers and targetable by calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory drugs acting on NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.
papers.summary: Open-label, single-arm exploratory trial in 19 patients with treatment-resistant depression receiving 6–12 sessions of 100-Hz magnetic seizure therapy targeting bilateral F3/F4, with clinical rating scales and 64-channel Go/Nogo task EEG before and after treatment. MST was associated with significant depressive symptom reduction (HAMD-24 40.53 to 22.53; response rates 42.1%–57.9%) and lower Nogo-related frontal theta activity at an uncorrected threshold, but EEG effects did not survive FDR correction and the uncontrolled design precludes mechanistic or biomarker conclusions.

papers.title: Optimizing aprocitentan dosing in elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension: a PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm modeling study.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated an integrated PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm model for aprocitentan and extrapolated it to elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension, predicting a 20.6% higher steady-state AUC than in healthy elderly Caucasians (52.5% higher with mild hepatic impairment). Simulations identified 6.25 mg once daily and midday (12:00-13:00) administration as candidate regimens, with predicted systolic/diastolic BP reductions of about 13.0/9.0 mmHg.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: A 39-item REDCap survey compared stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) practices across 66 epilepsy centers in North America (n=38) and Europe (n=28). North American centers used robotic implantation more often and had less SEEG experience and fewer dedicated readers, whereas European centers more frequently used SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation; unadjusted hemorrhage differences lost significance after adjustment for experience and volume.

papers.title: Integrative therapies for symptom management in dementia from a palliative perspective: narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.summary: Narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses on integrative care therapies for dementia symptom management from a palliative perspective. Cognitive stimulation had the highest evidence certainty (high for communication and social interaction; moderate for cognition, quality of life, and challenging behaviors), music therapy showed moderate-certainty benefit for depression but not agitation, and most other modalities had low-to-very-low certainty evidence.

papers.title: [Combined use of endocrine therapy with Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer: A retrospective real-world cohort study].
papers.journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
papers.summary: Retrospective real-world cohort of 41 castration-resistant prostate cancer patients compared standard endocrine therapy alone versus combined Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules. Median overall survival was 22.0 vs 34.0 months without statistical significance (P=0.094), but the combination significantly improved TCM syndrome scores and sleep quality (ISI 12.60→5.85 vs 12.29→12.43; all interaction P<0.01) and showed an OS benefit in the Gleason ≥9 subgroup.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sleep deprivation in nursing technicians working in shifts.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 198 nursing technicians at a Brazilian university hospital found a 43.9% prevalence of sleep deprivation (<5 hours/night). Associated factors included prolonged daily work hours (OR=3.60), anxiety symptoms (OR=6.58), coffee consumption (OR=3.14), inadequate fruit/vegetable intake (OR=2.25), and higher BMI (OR=1.27).

papers.title: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in an elderly female: A video-based case report and literature review.
papers.summary: Reports an 81-year-old woman who developed opsoclonus, myoclonus, ataxia, behavioral changes, and sleep disturbance, diagnosed with idiopathic OMAS after unremarkable laboratory and imaging workup and no tumor detected on follow-up. She improved markedly with steroid immunotherapy plus clonazepam and gabapentin, with no recurrence or malignancy at two-year follow-up, accompanied by video documentation and a literature review.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Council on Lifestyle and Cardiometabolic Health; Council on Arteriosclerosis, Thrombosis and Vascular Biology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Radiology and Intervention; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Council on Quality of Care and Outcomes Research
papers.summary: This AHA scientific statement evaluates cardiovascular health among US veterans using the Life's Essential 8 framework expanded to include mental health and substance use, reviewing guideline recommendations, barriers, and major VA programs across domains. It reports that veterans receiving VA care often achieve outcomes equal to or better than non-VA counterparts, reflecting strengths in coordinated team-based care, while identifying remaining opportunities to improve lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, and sleep disorder management.

papers.title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
papers.summary: This review summarizes aeromedical cardiovascular assessment of aircrew, integrating ICAO, EASA, FAA, and Turkish DGCA standards with European Society of Cardiology guidance across conditions including hypertension, coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, valvular disease, and devices. It reports that preserved ventricular function, low arrhythmic/thromboembolic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity generally support certification, whereas uncontrolled hypertension, reduced ejection fraction, malignant arrhythmias, or severe valvular/aortic disease usually preclude it.

papers.title: Social media-related dietary behaviors and integrated behavioral model constructs among university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 385 King Khalid University undergraduates, the study examined social media-related dietary behaviors using the Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM). Positive attitude, physical activity, and moderate social media use (1–2 or 3–4 hours/day) were associated with higher Dietary Habits scores, and the regression model explained 57.6% of variance.

papers.title: Can COVID-19 Cause Acute Psychosis in Pediatric Patients? A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 14-year-old female with no psychiatric history who developed acute psychosis with visual hallucinations two weeks after COVID-19 infection, improving on chlorpromazine and returning to school over two months. It highlights that COVID-19-associated acute psychosis, though rare, can occur in pediatric patients and that clinicians should test for COVID-19 and consider organic causes in new-onset psychosis.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
